current_bottleneck: The 293 family now appears to need a stronger explicit path-shape support object rather than another latent. 293d showed that explicit coarse support is directionally better than latent scaffolds for cointegration and mean-reversion structure, but the current coarse-code head is too weak and the branch still cannot control level-law fidelity, regime width timing, or jump ordering strongly enough.
last_result_summary: Iteration 136 completed the 293d-v0 experiment. The explicit coarse path support object improved the family relative to 293c: score 4/11, change KS recovered to 25/25, cointegration passed again, aggregate MR ratio rose to 0.093, and active-cell MR corr rose to 0.773. But level KS stayed at 1/25, regime differentiation stayed dead, jump realism remained far from gate, and coarse-code accuracy stayed low.
next_step_recommendation: Do post-experiment analysis comparing 293b, 293c, and 293d to decide whether the family should strengthen the explicit support object or whether even explicit coarse support is too weak to fix path shape.
current_best_model: 277d-v0, 279a-v0, 281a-v0, 281b-v0, and 282b-v0 are the current overall co-frontiers at 5/11 in the two-level reset.
current_best_note: 282b is still the cleanest current Stage B objective frontier at 5/11, but 284b and 285a strengthen the conclusion that the real cap is now the Stage A support object rather than the Stage B weighting law.
